core_obligations: Reduce to the scheme-theoretically dominant case and to a dense-open equality via accepted semi-continuity.
Build the dominating diagram W -> W -> V via map-of-components, flat base change and equidimensionality.
Expand all dimensions definitionally and convert to the scheme invariant via the two base changes of W -> W.
Prove the scheme statement: integral replacement, constancy, flatification, relative-dimension lemma.
proof_roadmap: dominance reduction + dominating diagram + definitional expansions + scheme recall
difficulty_reason: 170-line proof fully executed, the chapter's largest span: replace X by the scheme-theoretic image and reduce to the dense-open equality via the in-pool accepted semi-continuity (1); quasi-compactify via two named stack lemmas; find an irreducible scheme-theoretically dominant open V of a smooth cover via the in-pool accepted map-of-components; preserve dominance under flat base change (named lemma), scheme-ify, choose a dominating component C, open-ify to W, and keep dimensions unchanged via the in-pool accepted equidimensionality; expand all relative dimensions definitionally through the diagram (fibre-of-base-change is base-change-of-fibre), transfer the spaces-level formula (external-carried, named-pointer rank), base-change W -> W twice to convert fibre differences into the single invariant dim_w W_v - dim_w W + dim_v V; reduce to the scheme statement and recall its full proof: integral replacements, constancy of dim_w W_v, affine finite-type replacement, flatification via the flat base-change dominance lemma, and closure on the named relative-dimension lemma. No omissions.
